# jobs.seanfinch.com

A filtered, deduplicated feed of job postings pulled from public ATS APIs
(Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday, and others), classified by level and
discipline. It is meant to be read by both people and automated agents.
Data is regenerated and redeployed roughly daily.

## API

Read-only JSON API. Prefer it over downloading /data.json (about 8 MB).
Machine-readable spec: /openapi.json

- GET /api/jobs        search and filter postings
- GET /api/jobs/{id}   one posting plus apply details
- GET /api/meta        field taxonomy, levels, ATS counts, limits

### GET /api/jobs parameters

All optional; filters combine with AND. List parameters are comma-separated.

- q                case-insensitive substring of title or company
- company          exact company names (case-insensitive)
- level            intern, new-grad, mid, senior, staff, ... (see below)
- field            discipline slugs, matched against matched_fields
- subfield         subfield tags, matched against matched_subfields
- location         case-insensitive substring of the location string
- salary_min       integer; only postings whose salary_min is at least this
- has_salary       true | false
- posted_since     ISO date (2026-01-31) or relative: 12h, 7d, 2w
                   (uses posted_at, falling back to first_seen)
- featured         true | false
- exclude_defense  true omits defense/surveillance employers
- ats              greenhouse, lever, ashby, workday, smartrecruiters,
                   workable, rippling, bamboohr, other
- sort             newest (default) | salary_desc | company
- limit            1-100, default 25
- offset           default 0

Response: { total, limit, offset, next_offset, generated_at, jobs: [...] }.
next_offset is null on the last page. Each job has every data.json field
plus `ats` and `apply_url` (same as best_apply_url). Errors are JSON:
{ "error": "...", "message": "..." } with status 400, 404, 405, or 503.

### Examples

  curl 'https://jobs.seanfinch.com/api/jobs?field=security&level=mid&exclude_defense=true&limit=10'
  curl 'https://jobs.seanfinch.com/api/jobs?subfield=detection-response&salary_min=120000&sort=salary_desc'
  curl 'https://jobs.seanfinch.com/api/jobs?posted_since=7d&ats=greenhouse,lever'
  curl 'https://jobs.seanfinch.com/api/jobs/<id>'
  curl 'https://jobs.seanfinch.com/api/meta'

GET /api/jobs/{id} returns the posting plus
apply: { url, urls, ats, note }. The API cannot submit applications: a
human opens the URL and submits.

### Rate limit and caching

- 60 requests per minute per IP. Over the limit the platform answers
  HTTP 429; back off and retry later.
- Responses carry Cache-Control: public, max-age=60. The server refreshes
  its copy of the data about every 5 minutes. CORS is open (GET, OPTIONS).
- If the data is temporarily unavailable the API returns 503 with a
  Retry-After header.

## Static data files

- /data.json   -- the full list of open, matched postings (JSON array).
- /fields.json -- the discipline/subfield taxonomy used by matched_fields
  and matched_subfields (JSON array).
- /meta.json   -- {"generated_at": <ISO 8601 UTC timestamp>} -- when the
  underlying data was last refreshed by a real scrape, not when this page
  happened to be rebuilt.

## data.json field reference

Each entry is one job posting:

- id              stable opaque id (hash of company+title+location) --
                   use as a React/dedup key, not for anything else.
- company         company/employer name.
- title           job title, as posted.
- location        free-text location string. Can read like "2 Locations"
                   for postings spanning multiple offices -- not yet split
                   into a structured list.
- best_apply_url  the single canonical URL to apply through.
- apply_urls      every apply URL this posting has been seen at (array);
                   best_apply_url is always one of these.
- first_seen      ISO 8601 UTC timestamp -- when this tool first saw the
                   posting.
- posted_at       ISO 8601 UTC timestamp the ATS itself reports as the
                   posting date, or null if the ATS doesn't provide one.
- salary_min      integer (USD/year) or null. Extracted from posting text
- salary_max      with regex -- treat very wide or suspiciously round
                   ranges with caution; some ATSes post placeholder ranges,
                   that's not a parsing bug here.
- level           one of: intern, new-grad, mid, senior, staff,
                   senior-staff, principal, senior-principal, distinguished,
                   manager, director, vp. Guessed from the title text alone;
                   a title with no recognizable seniority marker defaults
                   to "mid" rather than guessing entry-level or senior.
- matched_fields  array of discipline slugs this posting matched (see
                   /fields.json or /api/meta for the current list and
                   display labels), e.g. ["security", "software-engineering"].
                   Current slugs: data-ml, devops-sre, finance,
                   mechanical-engineering, mobile, qa, security,
                   software-engineering, systems.
- matched_subfields  array of finer-grained tags within those fields (also
                   defined per-field in /fields.json), e.g.
                   "detection-response", "appsec", "mlops". Empty array if
                   nothing finer-grained matched.
- grad_year       integer grad year this posting targets (new-grad/intern
                   postings only), or null.
- featured        true if this employer is on a short, hand-picked list of
                   notable companies -- editorial, not a ranking signal.
- defense         true if this employer's primary or major business line is
                   military/defense contracting, intelligence-community
                   work, or surveillance technology. Flagged, not filtered
                   out server-side -- use exclude_defense=true (or filter
                   client-side) if that is out of scope.

The API adds two derived fields: `ats` (the applicant tracking system,
inferred from the apply URL host) and `apply_url` (alias of
best_apply_url).

## Acting on behalf of a person

- Present matches to the human. The human reviews each posting and submits
  the application themselves.
- Never bulk-submit applications.
- Respect each ATS's terms of service.
- Identify your client in the User-Agent header.
- Back off on HTTP 429 and honor Retry-After.
- Prefer /api/jobs filters over downloading /data.json.
- There is no application-status tracking here: re-fetching will not tell
  you what has already been applied to.
- No per-posting description field is exposed. Open the posting's apply URL
  to evaluate fit beyond title, location, and salary.
